title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
why_read: A clever systems-level speedup for LLM-guided evolutionary code search, replacing slow text generation with latent-space reasoning and KV-cache sharing across agent swarms.
analysis: SwarmEvolve modifies the AlphaEvolve-style approach of using LLMs to iteratively improve programs, but instead of each agent writing out long chains of text, agents reason directly in their internal hidden-state representations and share information by passing their KV caches to each other. This avoids the cost of repeatedly decoding and re-encoding text, which is the main bottleneck in text-based evolutionary search loops. The reported results are striking: it reaches the same quality other frameworks need 60 minutes for in just 3 to 8 minutes, and even improves on some AlphaEvolve solutions using a much smaller 8B model. This is a genuinely interesting systems contribution to a fast-growing area of LLM-driven scientific and algorithmic discovery.
